newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ECNZ plans power station job cuts to help compete.
newsitem.headline: ECNZ plans power station job cuts to help compete.

text.p: New Zealand state-owned power generating company ECNZ said on Wednesday it would have to cut 95 of 270 staff at its Huntly power station -- its largest thermal operation with output of 1,000 megawatts.
In a statement the company said the 1981-built steam turbine station had a thermal efficiency of 37 percent, compared with a typical rate for new gas turbine systems of nearer 60 percent.

"Reduced staff numbers is one of the outcomes of a wide ranging series of investigations and staff consultation aimed at cutting costs by NZ$9.0 million a year so the station can compete with new low-cost electricity generators," ECNZ added.

It estimated just under half the staff, in engineering and labouring, would be re-employed on 12-month contracts through separate companies tendering for service contracts at the station. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
